content.text:
You are a veteran Capcom NES pixel artist and art director for Mega Man 2-3. You are shown ONE small enemy sprite,
at 1x (true size, left) and enlarged with nearest-neighbour scaling (right), on a neutral grey-blue background
that is not part of the sprite.

The sprite is supposed to be this enemy:
"A small floating robot squid, Blooper-like, that swims along at and after Mega Man in pulses (tentacles gather, then thrust). It is a swimming mine: when it gets close its eyes flash red, then it explodes."
Intended size: about 16x16 to 20x20 px. Game: Mega Man 2-3 (NES).

Judge whether it is a convincing authentic NES Mega Man enemy that matches the description. Be calibrated:
authentic Capcom enemy sprites score about 90-95; competent fan art about 60-70; amateur or AI-looking pixel art
about 30-45. Do not reward or punish a sprite for being recognisable; judge what you see.

Criteria, 0-10 each:
- authenticity: could ship unchanged in MM2/MM3 (Capcom conventions, not "modern pixel art")
- description_fidelity: matches the description (body, features, role)
- readability_1x: the silhouette and features read instantly at true size
- pixel_craft: 1-px black outlines used the Capcom way, clean clusters, no jaggies, orphans, dithering or noise
- palette_discipline: NES colours, flat shading with at most one highlight, about 3 colours + transparent per 8x8 tile
- appeal: charm and character in the Capcom manner

Return ONLY a JSON object:
{"subscores": {"authenticity": n, "description_fidelity": n, "readability_1x": n, "pixel_craft": n,
  "palette_discipline": n, "appeal": n},
 "score": 0-100 overall,
 "verdict": "convincing" or "not_convincing",
 "issues": ["specific, located problems"],
 "fixes": ["specific pixel-level fixes"]}

message.content: {"subscores":{"authenticity":4,"description_fidelity":6,"readability_1x":5,"pixel_craft":5,"palette_discipline":6,"appeal":5},"score":52,"verdict":"not_convincing","issues":["At 1x, the mantle, face, and tentacles merge into a busy cyan-pink-black mass; the squid silhouette is not immediate.","The upper-right eye area is obscured by a large black cavity, while the lone red pixel appears detached rather than like a flashing eye.","The long pink horizontal band across the lower body reads as a mouth or platform instead of gathered tentacles.","The right-side pink-and-cyan projection resembles an arm, gun, or tail, weakening the compact floating-mine concept.","Black regions are excessively thick and irregular around the face and underside, unlike the controlled one-pixel contouring typical of Mega Man 2-3.","Several clusters form awkward hooks and single-pixel steps, especially at the upper-right rim, lower-left pink tip, and bottom tentacles.","Pink occupies too much of the mantle as an additional large colour mass rather than a restrained NES highlight or warning accent.","The sprite has more internal detail and competing colour regions than a small Capcom enemy would usually carry at this scale."],"fixes":["Simplify the mantle into a rounded 12-14-pixel-wide dome with a consistent one-pixel black outer contour.","Replace the upper-right black cavity with two clearly paired 1-2-pixel eyes; reserve red versions of those same pixels for the warning frame.","Remove the detached red pixel and keep all eye pixels enclosed by the face or outline.","Break the lower pink band into three or four distinct tentacle clusters, then create a second animation frame where those clusters pull inward.","Shorten or remove the right-side projection so the silhouette remains radial and squid-like rather than directional.","Reduce the palette to black, one pale cyan, one stronger cyan or pink accent, and transparency within each sprite tile; use red only in the flashing-eye frame.","Clean the lower contour into deliberate two- and three-pixel runs, eliminating isolated tips and uneven staircase patterns.","Make the mine function readable through animation: neutral cyan eyes, a red-eye warning frame, then a compact bright explosion frame."]}
